L2:
Short explanations, written in plain language.

Q: Explain in your own words why a bicycle stays upright while it is moving.
A: A moving bicycle keeps correcting itself. When it begins to lean to one side, the front wheel turns slightly into the lean, which steers the wheels back underneath the rider's weight. The faster it travels, the smaller and quicker those corrections are, so the bicycle feels steady.

Q: Explain in your own words why a lighthouse can be seen from far out at sea.
A: A lighthouse is built high up so that its beam clears the curve of the horizon. Lenses and mirrors gather the lamp's light and squeeze it into a narrow horizontal beam instead of letting it spread in every direction. Because the light is concentrated and starts from a height, a ship many miles away still receives enough of it to see the flash.

L4:
Answers that combine two unrelated subjects, using one to explain the other.

Task: Describe a barbershop organised as a court of law. Say which part of court procedure each step of the haircut copies and what it does for the customer.
Answer: The consultation is the arraignment: the customer states what he is charged with wanting and the barber reads it back to him, so there is no dispute later about what was agreed. The mirror on the far wall serves as the public gallery, since every cut is made in view and can be objected to while it is still reversible. Scissors and clippers act as opposing counsel, one arguing for length and the other for shape, and the barber alternates between them until neither has a further submission. Sweeping the floor is the sealing of the record: once the hair is gone the case cannot be reopened, and the customer settles costs on the way out.

Task: Describe a village postal route as a knitting pattern. Say which knitting instruction each part of the route copies and what it does for the postman.
Answer: The main road is the cast-on row: it fixes how many houses the whole route will carry, and everything after it hangs from that count. Each side lane is a purl stitch worked in the opposite direction, so the postman doubles back and the fabric of the route lies flat instead of curling into wasted mileage. Houses that receive post only on certain days are slipped stitches, passed over without being worked but still counted, which keeps the rhythm of the walk even. The return to the sorting office is the cast-off, binding the loose end so that tomorrow's round can start from the same edge.

L5:
Proposals for things that do not exist yet, each written by the person who thought of it.

Task: Invent a new kind of doorbell that does not exist today, and explain what problem it solves and how it works.
Proposal: An ordinary doorbell tells you that somebody is at the door but nothing about how much the visit matters, so a household either answers everything or ignores everything. This doorbell replaces the button with a weighted pull-cord: the harder the visitor pulls, the longer the chime sustains, and the mechanism holds that pull on a small dial inside the hall. A courier leaving a parcel gives a light tug that produces one short note, while a neighbour with something urgent pulls hard and sets off a chime that runs for several seconds. Because the effort is physical and the visitor can feel how hard they are pulling, the signal stays honest, and the household can decide whether to get up from the sound alone.

Task: Invent a new kind of suitcase that does not exist today, and explain what problem it solves and how it works.
Proposal: Travellers repack at the airport because they cannot tell which part of the case is over the weight limit until the whole thing is on the scale. This suitcase is built from four stacked drawers, each on its own spring-loaded floor that sinks as it fills and shows a coloured band through a slot in the shell. A drawer that dips past its band is holding more than a quarter of the allowance, so the owner can see which layer to lighten without opening anything. The springs also lock the drawers once the lid is closed, so the load stays balanced and the case does not tip when it is stood upright.
